title: bug: qa_reject, request_replan and release_task echo agent-written reasons into system chat lines with mention parsing on, so an at-token in a reason pages seats (task-85df8bf0 fixed only the step notice)
description:
This row follows up task-85df8bf0's QA review, which says: "amendPlanStep, qaReject, requestReplan and the claim notice title can still echo agent text; the worker listed them as follow-ups". The Serena memory gotcha-plan-step-text-at-tokens-echoed-as-mentions also lists these sites as STILL OPEN. The claim title is covered by task-df34243e. amend_plan_step is left out because its line carries a deliberate assignee tag and needs a split-post design.

Evidence at HEAD 119fce99 (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/):
- qaReject.ts:368 posts `QA rejected: ${params.reason}` through state.postSystemMessage with no options.
- requestReplan.ts:90 posts `Replan requested${stepHint}: ${reasonSummary}` the same way.
- releaseTask.ts posts to both #general and #workers:
  - :356-369: `🔓 <actor> released task: <title><reasonSuffix>`, plus the handoff's done/remains summaries;
  - :251-254: the 🔧 auto-route line.

How such a line pages seats:
- state/chatStore.ts:196 parses mentions unless the post passes parseMentions false.
- A recorded at-token takes a #general line out of the feed (util/chatPayload.ts:54).
- MentionRouter.routeSystemMessage (util/mentionRouter.ts:255-267) routes a line that has no KNOWN mention to every busy seat. A role tag pages its whole group.
- A #workers line is never feed, so release_task's mention-less #workers copy already pages every busy seat on each release.

Seen in .moe/messages:
- qa_reject echoed a role tag twice (2026-07-31 'worker'; 2026-10-26 'governors' on task-7a0b1881).
- release_task echoed 'governors' into three channels (2026-07-31 23:43:51Z).
Reasons routinely quote code, such as Kotlin/Java annotations and npm scopes, which parse as at-tokens.

Fix pattern: task-85df8bf0 added SystemPostOptions { parseMentions: false } (state/chatStore.ts:394-414), and completeStep.ts:143 uses it. None of these three sites has a deliberate tag of its own.

Files: qaReject.ts, requestReplan.ts, releaseTask.ts and one NEW test file under packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/. No open row's plan names any of them (checked at 119fce99).
definitionOfDone: qa_reject's 'QA rejected: <reason>', request_replan's 'Replan requested…: <reason>' and release_task's released and auto-route lines (both #general and #workers copies) are posted with { parseMentions: false }: an at-token in a reason, title or handoff summary records mentions [] and routes to no seat.
The text of every posted line is byte-identical to today's, and no MCP tool response or contract changes.

A NEW test file under packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/ drives each of the three tools with an at-token in its free text (the at-sign built at runtime, never spelled in source) and asserts the posted messages carry mentions [] and empty routing targets; restoring today's call fails each case, and existing qaReject/releaseTask tests pass unchanged.
In a snapshot outside the shared checkout: cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/qaReject.test.ts src/tools/releaseTask.test.ts <new test file> && npx tsc --noEmit exits 0.

The line `🔧 task task-1 was unassigned but stuck in WORKING; auto-routed to REVIEW` is unaddressed in #general and in #workers. It names no one, so the #general copy is feed with or without the option: also spy (call-through) on h.state.postToGeneral and assert it was called with (line, { parseMentions: false }).
(e) The helper stays opt-in. h.state.postToRoleChannel('workers', content), with content naming worker-busy, records ['worker-busy'] and routes to ['worker-busy']. The same call with { parseMentions: false } records [] and routes to [].
